origin.description: Lines for the top of an R HTML help page.
origin.usage: HTMLheader(title = "R", logo = TRUE, up = NULL, top = file.path(Rhome, "doc/html/index.html"), Rhome = "", css = file.path(Rhome, "doc/html/R.css"), headerTitle = paste("R:", title), outputEncoding = "UTF-8")

arguments.name: up
arguments.text: Link for the up arrow, or NULL.

arguments.name: Rhome
arguments.text: Prefix for the logo, CSS, and arrows.

origin.details: Writes a doctype, a UTF-8 content-type unless another encoding is given, the CSS link, the title, and optional arrows.
origin.value: A character vector of HTML lines.
origin.example: HTMLheader("Hello", logo = FALSE, up = NULL, top = NULL, Rhome = "")

translation.description: Lines for the top of an R HTML help page.
translation.usage: html_header(title="R", logo=True, up=None, top="", rhome="", css=None, header_title=None, output_encoding="UTF-8")

arguments.name: up
arguments.text: Link for the up arrow, or NULL.

arguments.name: Rhome
arguments.text: Prefix for the logo, CSS, and arrows.

translation.details: An empty rhome still starts those links with /, because R's file.path does. Charset aliases such as latin1 and utf8 are rewritten.
translation.example:
from tools import html_header
print("\n".join(html_header("Hello", logo=False, up=None, top=None, rhome="")))
